mainTopic: Lien-cancelling acts, a wife's right to her family's items, and whether a fetus of a כהן lets slaves eat תרומה
overview: The amud opens with the end of a rule from the previous discussion: like הקדש and חמץ, freeing a slave cancels a creditor's lien. Next, רב יהודה rules that a wife can take back her dowry items that rose in value. She takes one as her כתובה and may even pay for the other, because of שבח בית אביה. Then a new משנה begins. רבי יוסי rules that if a כהן dies and leaves his בת ישראל wife pregnant, her slaves may not eat תרומה, because the fetus owns a share and a fetus disqualifies but does not enable. The גמרא asks for his reason. רבה says a fetus inside a non-כהן mother counts as a non-כהן. רב יוסף says an unborn child cannot let others eat. A ברייתא is brought that challenges רב יוסף, and the challenge stands as a קשיא. שמואל reports that the חכמים disagree with רבי יוסי, though שמואל himself agrees with him. A ברייתא then sets out the cases of children, a fetus, and the two kinds of slaves, together with the views of רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי and רבי שמעון בן יוחי. The amud ends in the middle of explaining רבי שמעון's view, and the explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Freeing a slave cancels a lien
steps.stepSummary: The last words of a principle from the previous discussion: שחרור, freeing a slave, removes a creditor's lien, just like הקדש and חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: And freeing a slave cancels the lien on him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a sentence it started just before: certain acts cancel a creditor's claim on an item. This closes the earlier discussion about the robe that was placed on the dead husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full rule is that הקדש, חמץ on פסח, and שחרור all cancel a שעבוד. Once an item becomes forbidden or legally changes status, the creditor can no longer collect from it. This is why the robe, now forbidden because it was used for the dead, is released from the lien.

keyTerms.meaning: Freeing a slave
They cancel / remove
A lien, a creditor's legal claim on property

steps.whatToRemember: Some acts change an item's status so completely that a creditor's lien on it falls away.

phrases.english: And freeing a slave — these cancel a lien.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the principle used in the previous discussion of the robe.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: הקדש, חמץ, and שחרור cancel a lien, so the robe is released from the creditors.

steps.title: The wife's two belongings that rose in value
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that a wife who brought two items worth 1,000 that rose to 2,000 takes one for her כתובה and may pay for the other and take it too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: If she brought her husband two items worth one thousand זוז, and they went up in value to two thousand, she takes one as her כתובה, and she pays money for the other and takes it, because they are her family's pride.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives a new ruling about a wife collecting her dowry items. She can take one item as her כתובה and buy the second one back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her כתובה only covers the original 1,000, so one item, now worth 1,000, pays it off. The second item really belongs to the husband's side, but she may pay its value and take it. The reason is שבח בית אביה: items from her father's house carry family pride, so she gets first right to them.

keyTerms.meaning: She brought into the marriage
They went up in value
Her marriage contract payment
She pays money for it
The pride of her father's house, family heirlooms

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:

phrases.aramaic: הִכְנִיסָה לוֹ שְׁנֵי כֵלִים בְּאֶלֶף זוּז,
phrases.english: If she brought him two items worth a thousand zuz,
and they went up in value and reached two thousand,
one she takes as her ketubah,
and the other one she pays its value and takes it,
because of the pride of her father's house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ruling about how a wife collects her dowry items.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: She takes one item as her כתובה and may pay for the second and take it, because of שבח בית אביה.

steps.title: Why repeat this ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רב יהודה adds, since he already taught that שבח בית אביה belongs to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us? That her family's pride belongs to her? רב יהודה already said that once!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה's ruling as unnecessary. He already gave a ruling based on the same idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes a teacher does not repeat the same rule for no reason. If שבח בית אביה was already taught, this new statement seems to add nothing. The challenge forces the גמרא to find something new in it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us?
Hers
One time, already once

phrases.english: What is he teaching us —
that the pride of her father's house is hers?

phrases.aramaic: הָא אַמְרַהּ רַב יְהוּדָה חֲדָא זִימְנָא!
phrases.english: But Rav Yehuda already said that once!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 2 as repeating something already taught.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The idea of שבח בית אביה was already taught by רב יהודה, so this ruling looks repeated and unnecessary.

steps.title: The new point: she may even pay to take it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the new ruling teaches she may pay money and take the extra item, not only collect it as her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: that rule only applies when she comes to take it as her כתובה, but to pay money and take it, no. So he teaches us that she may.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing what is new here. Without this ruling, we might have limited her right to items she collects for her כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Collecting her own כתובה is something she is already owed, so giving her the family items there is easy. Paying to take an item that goes beyond what she is owed is a bigger step. רב יהודה teaches that שבח בית אביה is strong enough to give her this right too.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said
These words apply only
To pay money and take

steps.whatToRemember: שבח בית אביה lets the wife take back family items even by paying for them, not only by collecting her כתובה.

phrases.english: You might have said:
these words apply only where
she comes to take it as her ketubah,
but to pay money and take it — no,
so he teaches us that she may.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3 by pointing out the new detail in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the second statement adds a new detail beyond the first.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Her right to family items only applies when she collects them as her כתובה, not when she must pay extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: She may also pay the value and take the extra family item.

steps.title: A pregnant widow of a כהן and her slaves eating תרומה
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: if a בת ישראל married to a כהן is widowed while pregnant, her slaves may not eat תרומה, since the unborn child owns a share and a fetus does not give the right to eat. This is רבי יוסי's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A בת ישראל who married a כהן, and he died and left her pregnant: her slaves may not eat תרומה, because of the unborn child's share, since a fetus can disqualify but does not give the right to eat. These are the words of רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new case. It rules that the pregnant widow's slaves may not eat תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The slaves are part of the dead כהן's estate, so the unborn child owns a share in them as an heir. A fetus can take away someone's right to eat תרומה, but it cannot give anyone that right. So even though the father was a כהן, the slaves may not eat because of the fetus's share.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה, the start of a new משנה
Pregnant
The holy portion of produce only כהנים and their household may eat
An unborn child, a fetus
Disqualifies
Enables someone to eat

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the slaves may eat because the father was a כהן. The fetus is a כהן too, but a fetus never gives anyone the right to eat תרומה.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
An Israelite woman who married a priest, and he died,
and left her pregnant —
her slaves may not eat teruma,
because of the share of the fetus,
for the fetus disqualifies,
and does not enable eating; these are the words of Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנִּיסֵּת לְכֹהֵן וּמֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The pregnant widow's slaves may not eat תרומה because the fetus owns a share, and a fetus disqualifies but does not enable eating (רבי יוסי).

steps.title: The Sages extend the ruling to a priest's daughter
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים tell רבי יוסי: since you testified about a בת ישראל married to a כהן, the same should be true of a בת כהן married to a כהן who died and left her pregnant. Her slaves should not eat תרומה because of the fetus's share.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Since you told us about an Israelite woman married to a כהן, then also a כהן's daughter married to a כהן who died and left her pregnant: her slaves should not eat תרומה, because the fetus owns a share.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes with the חכמים answering רבי יוסי. They say his ruling should also cover a pregnant widow who is herself a בת כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason is the same: the unborn baby owns part of the slaves, and an unborn baby does not let them eat. So the חכמים see no difference between a mother who is a בת ישראל and a mother who is a בת כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: You testified, meaning you reported a ruling you received from your teachers
A woman born to a כהן, who may eat תרומה on her own
Pregnant
The fetus's share in the father's estate

phrases.english: They said to him: Since you testified before us
phrases.notes: "They" are the חכמים, and "him" is רבי יוסי from the previous step.

phrases.english: about an Israelite woman married to a כהן,
then also a כהן's daughter married to a כהן, and he died
and left her pregnant:
her slaves may not eat תרומה,
because of the fetus's share.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the משנה by having the חכמים apply רבי יוסי's ruling to a second case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, the slaves of a pregnant widow who is a בת כהן also may not eat תרומה, because of the fetus's share.

steps.title: What is רבי יוסי's real reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוסי rules this way. One option is that a fetus inside a non-כהן mother counts as a non-כהן. The other option is that only a born child lets others eat תרומה, and an unborn child does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: Is רבי יוסי's reason that a fetus inside a non-כהן woman counts as a non-כהן? Or perhaps a born child lets others eat, and an unborn child does not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה. It asks which of two possible reasons stands behind רבי יוסי's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reason one is about the baby's status: while the baby is inside a בת ישראל, it is treated like part of her, so it is not yet a כהן. Reason two grants that the baby is a כהן, but holds that an unborn child cannot give others the right to eat. Both reasons lead to the same result in the משנה's case, so the גמרא needs to look for a case where they differ.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked before the scholars
A fetus inside a non-כהן woman counts as a non-כהן
A child who has been born lets others eat תרומה
Or perhaps

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two reasons. Reason one says the fetus is not a כהן at all. Reason two says the fetus is a כהן but still cannot let others eat until it is born.

phrases.english: GEMARA: A question was asked of them:
Is the reason of רבי יוסי

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּקָסָבַר עוּבָּר בִּמְעֵי זָרָה — זָר הוּא,
phrases.english: because he holds that a fetus in the womb of a non-כהן woman is a non-כהן,
or perhaps: one who is born lets others eat,
and one who is not born does not let others eat?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of רבי יוסי's ruling from the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which reasoning lies behind רבי יוסי's ruling: the status of a fetus inside a non-כהן mother, or the rule that an unborn child cannot let others eat.

steps.title: Where do the two reasons give different results?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the two reasons. The answer is a fetus inside a בת כהן: what is the law there?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the practical difference? A fetus inside a כהן's daughter. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to the case where the two reasons split. This sets up the answers of רבה and רב יוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a בת כהן mother, reason one does not apply, because the mother is not a non-כהן, so the slaves could eat. Reason two still applies, because the baby is still unborn, so the slaves could not eat. This is exactly the case the חכמים raised in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the practical difference?
A woman from a כהן family

phrases.english: What is the practical difference?
A fetus in the womb of a כהן's daughter: what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the test case that separates the two reasons from step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The case where the two possible reasons lead to different laws.

steps.title: רבה: the fetus counts as a non-כהן
steps.stepSummary: רבה says רבי יוסי's reason is that a fetus inside a non-כהן mother counts as a non-כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: This is רבי יוסי's reason: he holds that a fetus inside a non-כהן woman is a non-כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the question by choosing the first reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבה, the problem in the משנה comes from the mother being a בת ישראל. So if the mother is a בת כהן, the fetus is a כהן and the slaves may eat. That means רבי יוסי would not agree with what the חכמים said in step 6.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the reason
An אמורא who gives the first answer

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה, הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
phrases.english: רבה said: This is the reason of רבי יוסי:

phrases.aramaic: דְּקָסָבַר עוּבָּר בִּמְעֵי זָרָה זָר הוּא.
phrases.english: he holds that a fetus in the womb of a non-כהן woman is a non-כהן.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה, הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The reason is the fetus's status: inside a non-כהן mother it is a non-כהן. So with a בת כהן mother, the slaves may eat.

steps.title: רב יוסף: an unborn child cannot let others eat
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says רבי יוסי's reason is that only a born child lets others eat תרומה, and an unborn child does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: One who is born lets others eat, and one who is not born does not.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף disagrees with רבה and chooses the second reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב יוסף, the mother's family does not matter at all. Any unborn baby blocks the slaves, so even with a בת כהן mother they may not eat, just as the חכמים said in step 6.

keyTerms.meaning: Lets others eat, here meaning it gives the slaves the right to eat תרומה
An אמורא who argues with רבה

phrases.english: רב יוסף said: One who is born lets others eat,
and one who is not born does not let others eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite answer to רבה's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The reason is that an unborn child cannot let others eat. So even with a בת כהן mother, the slaves may not eat.

steps.title: A ברייתא where רבי יוסי says he did not hear about a priest's daughter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב יוסף with a ברייתא. There, when the חכמים ask רבי יוסי about a בת כהן married to a כהן, he answers that he heard a ruling about the first case but not about this one.
steps.simpleTranslation: An objection was raised: They said to רבי יוסי: Since you told us about an Israelite woman married to a כהן, what is the law for a כהן's daughter married to a כהן? He said to them: This one I heard, and that one I did not hear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רב יוסף's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, רבי יוסי treats the two cases as different: he received a ruling about the בת ישראל but not about the בת כהן. That fits רבה, who says the mother's family matters. According to רב יוסף both cases are exactly the same, so it is hard to see why רבי יוסי would separate them.

keyTerms.meaning: An objection was raised, usually from a ברייתא or משנה
This one I heard, and that one I did not hear
What is the law?

steps.confusionAlert: In the משנה (step 6) the חכמים state that the בת כהן case is the same. In this ברייתא they only ask about it, and רבי יוסי answers that he has no tradition about the second case. He does not rule on it either way.

phrases.english: An objection was raised: They said to רבי יוסי:
Since you testified before us
about an Israelite woman married to a כהן,
what is the law for a כהן's daughter married to a כהן?
He said to them: This one I heard,
phrases.notes: "This one" is the בת ישראל case, which he received from his teachers.

phrases.english: and that one I did not hear.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's answer from step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's view that רבי יוסי's reason is that an unborn child cannot let others eat.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רב יוסף were right, the בת ישראל case and the בת כהן case would be the same. Yet רבי יוסי treats them as separate and says he heard a ruling only about the first. That fits רבה's view, where the mother's family makes a difference.

steps.title: רב יוסף's reason does not fit רבי יוסי's answer
steps.stepSummary: רבה's reason explains why רבי יוסי split the two cases. רב יוסף's reason makes both cases the same, so his answer 'this I heard, this I did not hear' makes no sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well if the reason is that a fetus inside a non-כהן mother counts as a non-כהן. That is why רבי יוסי told them: this case I heard, and this case I did not hear. But if the reason is that only a born child lets others eat and an unborn child does not, what could he mean by 'this I heard and this I did not hear'? It is exactly the same case!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge it started in step 11. It shows that רבי יוסי's answer fits רבה's reason but not רב יוסף's reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבה, the mother matters. A non-כהן mother is different from a בת כהן mother, so it makes sense that רבי יוסי heard a ruling about one case and not the other. According to רב יוסף, only being born matters, and an unborn child is unborn whoever the mother is, so the two cases should be identical.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well if you say... (sets up the reason that fits)
A fetus inside a non-כהן woman counts as a non-כהן
A born child lets others eat תרומה
It is the very same thing

phrases.english: It works well if you say:
a fetus inside a non-priest woman is a non-priest
that is why he said to them:
This I heard, and this I did not hear.
phrases.notes: The first case has a non-כהן mother. The second has a בת כהן mother, married to a כהן (step 11).

phrases.english: But if you say:
a born child lets others eat,
one not yet born does not let others eat,

phrases.aramaic: מַאי זוֹ שָׁמַעְתִּי וְזוֹ לֹא שָׁמַעְתִּי?
phrases.english: what does 'this I heard and this I did not hear' mean?
It is the very same case!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge from step 11 by explaining why the ברייתא hurts רב יוסף.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's explanation of רבי יוסי (step 10)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With רב יוסף's reason, the fetus's mother makes no difference. So רבי יוסי had no reason to say he heard one case and not the other.

steps.title: The challenge against רב יוסף stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא closes with one word: it is a difficulty. The question on רב יוסף stays unanswered.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a difficulty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits it has no answer for רב יוסף. The challenge stays in place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word קשיא means the question is strong and no answer was found. This leaves רבה's reason as the one that fits רבי יוסי's words.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a difficulty, a question left unanswered

steps.confusionAlert: קשיא here is not a new question. It is a verdict: the previous challenge stays unanswered.

phrases.english: It is a difficulty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge of steps 11 and 12 with no answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב יוסף's explanation is left with an unresolved difficulty.

steps.title: שמואל: the Sages disagree with רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the ruling is only רבי יוסי's view. The חכמים say the slaves eat תרומה through the dead man's children, or else his brothers, or else his whole family.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: This is the view of רבי יוסי. But the חכמים say: if the dead man has sons, the slaves eat because of the sons. If he has no sons, they eat because of his brothers. If he has no brothers, they eat because of his whole family.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement opens here. שמואל points out that רבי יוסי's ruling is not shared by everyone, and he gives the view of the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the חכמים, the slaves belong to whoever inherits the dead כהן: his sons, his brothers, or his wider family. All of these are כהנים, so the slaves may eat. The unborn fetus does not stop them.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the view of (only one opinion)
They eat because of (through the ownership of)
Family, the wider relatives who inherit

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
This is the view of Rabbi Yosei.
But the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ לוֹ בָּנִים — אוֹכְלִים מִשּׁוּם בָּנִים.
phrases.english: If he has sons, they eat because of the sons.
phrases.notes: 'He' is the dead כהן husband, and 'they' are his slaves.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לוֹ בָּנִים — אוֹכְלִים מִשּׁוּם אַחִים.
phrases.english: If he has no sons, they eat because of the brothers.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לוֹ אַחִים — אוֹכְלִים מִשּׁוּם מִשְׁפָּחָה כּוּלָּהּ.
phrases.english: If he has no brothers, they eat because of the whole family.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the reason behind רבי יוסי's view to the opposing view of the חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים let the slaves eat תרומה through the dead כהן's heirs. The fetus does not block them.

steps.title: Does שמואל reject רבי יוסי? He holds a fetus can acquire
steps.stepSummary: Saying 'this is רבי יוסי's view' sounds like שמואל disagrees. But שמואל publicly taught that a fetus acquires what is given to it, which fits רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'This is his view' sounds like שמואל does not hold it. But שמואל told רב חנא of Baghdad: Go bring me a group of ten men, so I can tell you in front of them: if someone gives something to a fetus, the fetus acquires it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that שמואל disagrees with רבי יוסי. It brings a ruling of שמואל that seems to agree with רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי treats the fetus as already owning a share of the estate. שמואל held that a fetus can acquire, and he wanted that ruling said in front of ten men so it would spread. So how could he reject רבי יוסי?

keyTerms.meaning: And he does not hold this way
A group of ten men
If one gives something to a fetus, it acquires it

phrases.english: 'This' — so he does not hold it?
But Shmuel said
to Rav Ḥana of Baghdad:
Go bring me a group of ten,
so I can tell you in front of them:
one who gives ownership to a fetus — it acquires.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״זוֹ״ וְלָא סְבִירָא לֵיהּ. הָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the hint in step 14 that שמואל rejects רבי יוסי.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication that שמואל disagrees with רבי יוסי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל elsewhere says a fetus acquires, which is the basis of רבי יוסי's view. So he should agree with רבי יוסי.

steps.title: שמואל agrees with רבי יוסי and is only reporting the dispute
steps.stepSummary: שמואל does hold like רבי יוסי. He said 'this is רבי יוסי's view' only to tell us that the חכמים argue with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, 'this is his view,' and שמואל does hold it. What is he teaching us? That the חכמים disagree with רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. שמואל agrees with רבי יוסי. His words were only meant to report that there is a dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'this is רבי יוסי's view' does not have to mean 'and I reject it.' Here it just tells us there is an argument. So there is no clash with שמואל's ruling about a fetus acquiring.

keyTerms.meaning: And he does hold this way
What is he teaching us?
They disagree

phrases.english: Rather: 'This,' and he does hold it.
What is he teaching us?
That the Rabbis disagree with Rabbi Yosei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15 by reading שמואל's words differently.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'This is רבי יוסי's view' meant שמואל rejects it.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל agrees with רבי יוסי. He is only telling us that the חכמים disagree.

steps.title: Do the Sages really disagree? They acknowledged רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רבי זכאי cites a source saying רבי יוסי testified in the name of שמעיה and אבטליון, and the חכמים acknowledged him. That sounds like they agreed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But do they really disagree? רבי זכאי objected: This was a testimony that רבי יוסי gave in the name of שמעיה and אבטליון, and they acknowledged him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions whether the חכמים really argue with רבי יוסי. It brings a source saying they acknowledged his testimony.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the חכמים acknowledged רבי יוסי's testimony, it seems they accepted his ruling. That would mean there is no dispute, against what שמואל just said.

keyTerms.meaning: But do they really disagree?
He raises an objection from a source
He gave testimony (reporting a ruling he received)
And they acknowledged him

phrases.english: But do they disagree?
Rabbi Zakkai objected:
This testimony Rabbi Yosei testified
from the mouths of Shemaya and Avtalyon,
and they acknowledged him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim from step 16 that the חכמים disagree with רבי יוסי.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's report that the חכמים argue with רבי יוסי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A source says the חכמים acknowledged רבי יוסי's testimony, which suggests they agreed with him.

steps.title: Acknowledging is not accepting
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the source does not say the חכמים 'accepted' the ruling. It says they 'acknowledged' it, meaning they found his reasoning sensible but still disagreed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Does it say 'and they accepted'? It says 'and they acknowledged him,' meaning his reasoning made sense.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the challenge by looking closely at one word in the source. The חכמים said his view was logical but did not adopt it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Accepting would mean the חכמים took on the ruling as law. Acknowledging only means they agreed it was a reasonable view. So the חכמים can still disagree, and שמואל's report stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Does the source say...?
And they accepted (as the law)
That his reasoning makes sense

steps.whatToRemember: רבה's reason (a fetus in a non-כהן mother counts as a non-כהן) fits רבי יוסי, and רב יוסף's reason is left with a קשיא. שמואל agrees with רבי יוסי but reports that the חכמים argue. The חכמים only found רבי יוסי's view sensible; they did not accept it.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'והודו לו' as 'they agreed with the ruling.' Here it means only that they saw the logic, not that they adopted it.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Does it teach 'and they accepted'?
It teaches 'and they acknowledged him,'
meaning his reasoning makes sense.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זכאי's challenge from step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Close reading of a single word
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'They acknowledged him' means the חכמים accepted רבי יוסי's ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'They acknowledged him' only means they found his reasoning sensible. They still disagree.

steps.title: A ברייתא: when the widow's slaves may eat תרומה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lays out three cases: the כהן left children, left a pregnant wife, or left both. In the last case only her own slaves eat, because the fetus has a share in the other slaves. This is רבי יוסי's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: If he left children, both kinds of slaves eat. If he left her pregnant, neither kind eats. If he left children and also left her pregnant, the slaves of מלוג eat just as she eats. The slaves of צאן ברזל do not eat, because of the fetus's share, since a fetus disqualifies but does not enable. These are the words of רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with the full set of cases about a dead כהן's slaves and תרומה. This explains רבי יוסי's view, which the last few steps were discussing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The slaves of מלוג belong to the wife, and she eats through her living children, so her slaves eat too. The slaves of צאן ברזל are inherited by the כהן's heirs, and the fetus is one of those heirs. A fetus does not give anyone the right to eat, but its share is enough to block the slaves from eating.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaves that are the wife's own property; the husband only uses them
Slaves the husband took full responsibility for, so they pass to his heirs
Pregnant
Disqualifies but does not enable someone to eat תרומה
The fetus's share in the inheritance

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of slaves. The wife's own slaves (מלוג) follow her. The צאן ברזל slaves follow the heirs, and the fetus is one of the heirs.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule 'a fetus disqualifies but does not enable' is the key to the rest of this sugya.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
If he left children, both these and those eat.
phrases.notes: 'These and those' means both kinds of slaves: hers (מלוג) and the ones the heirs get (צאן ברזל).

phrases.aramaic: הִנִּיחָהּ מְעוּבֶּרֶת — אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ אֵין אוֹכְלִים.
phrases.english: If he left her pregnant, both these and those do not eat.
If he left children and also left her pregnant,

phrases.aramaic: עַבְדֵי מְלוֹג אוֹכְלִים כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁהִיא אוֹכֶלֶת,
phrases.english: the slaves of מלוג eat, just as she eats,
but the slaves of צאן ברזל may not eat,
because of the fetus's share.
For a fetus disqualifies but does not enable eating.
These are the words of רבי יוסי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the full ברייתא behind רבי יוסי's view, which steps 14 to 18 were discussing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When there are children and a fetus, the wife's מלוג slaves eat, but the צאן ברזל slaves do not, because a fetus disqualifies and does not enable.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל reports a girl versus boy distinction
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי reports his father's view differently: a girl lets the slaves eat, but a boy does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל the son of רבי יוסי says in his father's name: A daughter enables eating. A son does not enable eating.
steps.whatsHappening: A second version of רבי יוסי's view is brought. It depends on whether the child is a girl or a boy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Daughters do not inherit when there are sons, so a girl takes no share and does not block the slaves. A boy does share the inheritance, and since he cannot enable, he blocks them. The idea that daughters get nothing alongside a son is stated openly in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of his father
Enables someone to eat תרומה

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם אָבִיו:
phrases.english: רבי ישמעאל the son of רבי יוסי says in the name of his father:
A daughter enables eating,
a son does not enable eating.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם אָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another report of רבי יוסי's view, splitting it by girl versus boy.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A daughter enables the slaves to eat, but a son does not.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן יוחי: sons yes, daughters no
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחי says that if there are sons, the slaves eat. If there are only daughters, they do not, because the fetus may be a boy and then he alone inherits.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן יוחי says: If there are males, they all eat. If there are females, they do not eat, in case the fetus turns out to be a male. Daughters get nothing where there is a son.
steps.whatsHappening: A third view is brought. It depends on whether the children already born are sons or daughters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the living children are daughters and the fetus turns out to be a boy, the boy takes everything, since daughters inherit nothing where there is a son. Then the only owner is a fetus, and a fetus cannot enable eating. So we do not let the slaves eat.

keyTerms.meaning: Males (sons)
Females (daughters)
In case it turns out to be
Daughters get nothing where there is a son

phrases.english: רבי שמעון בן יוחי says:
If there are males, all the slaves eat,
if there are females, they do not eat,
in case the fetus turns out to be male,
and daughters have nothing where there is a son.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third opinion on the same case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With living sons the slaves eat. With only daughters they do not, because a male fetus would take everything.

steps.title: Why worry about a boy, when a girl also blocks?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי שמעון needs the reason 'maybe the fetus is a boy.' Even a girl fetus would share with her sisters and block the slaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why specifically say 'in case the fetus turns out to be male'? He could get the same result from the fact that a female also disqualifies!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון's reasoning as more complicated than needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the living children are all daughters, a girl fetus also inherits together with them. Her share alone would block the slaves. So why does רבי שמעון bring in the case of a boy?

keyTerms.meaning: Why specifically this?
He could get it from another reason
She disqualifies

phrases.aramaic: מַאי אִירְיָא שֶׁמָּא יִמָּצֵא עוּבָּר זָכָר?
phrases.english: Why specifically 'in case the fetus turns out to be male'?
Let him get it from the fact that a female also disqualifies!
phrases.notes: He means a girl fetus. She would inherit along with her sisters, so her share alone blocks the slaves.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִירְיָא שֶׁמָּא יִמָּצֵא עוּבָּר זָכָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reason רבי שמעון gave in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's reason 'in case the fetus is male'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A simpler reason exists: a girl fetus also has a share and also disqualifies, so the boy case is not needed.

steps.title: He gave two reasons
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי שמעון meant two reasons: a girl fetus also blocks, and on top of that, a boy fetus would take everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is saying one reason and another. One: a female also disqualifies. And another: in case the fetus is male, and daughters have nothing where there is a son.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי שמעון agrees a girl blocks. He simply added a second reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Either way the slaves cannot eat. A girl fetus blocks with her share. A boy fetus is even worse, because he takes the entire inheritance, leaving only a fetus as owner.

keyTerms.meaning: He is saying one reason, and another one besides

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון, when the living children are daughters the slaves never eat, whether the fetus is a girl or a boy.

phrases.english: He is saying one reason and another:
One, that a female also disqualifies.
And another, in case the fetus turns out to be male,
and daughters have nothing where there is a son.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the statement as giving two reasons
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון's only reason was a male fetus, which suggests a female would not block.
steps.terutzMaskana: He agrees a female blocks, and he added the male case as an extra reason.

steps.title: But with sons, there is still a fetus
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about the first half of רבי שמעון's view: when there are sons, how can the slaves eat? The fetus might be a boy who shares with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If there are males, they eat': but there is a fetus!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון's first ruling, that with living sons the slaves eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A boy fetus would inherit together with his brothers. By רבי יוסי's rule, the fetus's share should block the slaves. So why do they eat?

keyTerms.meaning: But there is

phrases.english: 'If there are males, they eat':
phrases.notes: The גמרא is going back to the first half of רבי שמעון's statement from step 21.

phrases.english: But there is a fetus!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the daughters case to the sons case in רבי שמעון's statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's ruling that with living sons the slaves eat
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A male fetus would share with the sons, and a fetus's share should block the slaves.

steps.title: The answer begins: what רבי שמעון holds
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts its answer by explaining what רבי שמעון holds. The rest of the answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its answer. It is about to tell us a principle רבי שמעון holds, and that principle explains why the fetus does not block.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'he holds' shows that the answer will come from רבי שמעון's own legal view, not from changing the wording. The content of that view comes at the start of the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds (the opinion that)

phrases.english: He holds:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the challenge in step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining רבי שמעון's underlying principle (continues on the next amud)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The fetus's share should block the slaves even when there are sons.
steps.terutzMaskana: A principle held by רבי שמעון explains why it does not; the details follow on the next amud.
